title: Cursor pagination
description: Opaque forward-only cursor paging on every list operation, where the client passes `cursor` and the server returns `nextCursor`.
question: Does the framework follow the cursor, or stop after the first page?
why: This failure is quiet and severe: an adapter that ignores `nextCursor` reports a server's first page as its entire catalogue, so tools simply do not exist as far as the agent is concerned. The spec also warns that an empty-string cursor is valid and must not be read as the end.
usage_note: Not published. Candidate source: count of public MCP servers using this capability. Not estimated, so the panel stays empty until the corpus is scanned.

notes.crewai: CrewAI 1.15.26: `MCPServerAdapter` (through mcpadapt) calls `list_tools()` once with no cursor and ignores `nextCursor`. Against a 60-tool fixture served in pages of 20, the agent gets the first 20 tools and never learns the other 40 exist.
notes.google_adk: Google ADK 2.11.0: `McpToolset.get_tools` calls `list_tools()` once with no cursor and ignores `nextCursor`. Against a 60-tool fixture served in pages of 20, the agent gets the first 20 tools and never learns the other 40 exist.
notes.autogen: AutoGen 0.7.5: `McpWorkbench.list_tools` makes one `tools/list` request and ignores `nextCursor`, so only the first page (20 of 60 fixture tools) reaches the agent.
notes.semantic_kernel: Semantic Kernel 1.45.0: `load_tools` calls `list_tools()` once and never follows `nextCursor`, so only the first page (20 of 60 fixture tools) becomes functions.
notes.llamaindex: LlamaIndex (llama-index-tools-mcp 0.6.0): `McpToolSpec.fetch_tools` calls `list_tools()` once with no cursor and ignores `nextCursor`. Against a 60-tool fixture served in pages of 20, the agent gets the first 20 tools.
notes.google_adk_js: Google ADK (TypeScript) 2.2.1: `MCPToolset.getTools` calls `listTools()` once with no cursor and ignores `nextCursor`. Against 60 tools served in pages of 20, the agent gets the first 20.
notes.haystack: Haystack (mcp-haystack 1.5.2): `MCPClient` calls `list_tools()` once with no cursor and ignores `nextCursor`. Against a 60-tool fixture served in pages of 20, the toolset holds the first 20 tools.
notes.smolagents: smolagents 1.26.0 (mcpadapt 0.1.20): mcpadapt calls `list_tools()` once with no cursor and ignores `nextCursor`. Against a 60-tool fixture served in pages of 20, `MCPClient.get_tools()` returns the first 20 tools and the agent never learns the other 40 exist.
notes.dspy: DSPy 3.4.0: DSPy has no tool listing. Its documented pattern calls the caller's `session.list_tools()` once, which returns only the first page. All pages arrive only when the caller follows `nextCursor` on its own session, as the probe does.
notes.beeai: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85: `MCPTool.from_session` calls `session.list_tools()` once and ignores `nextCursor`, so against a 60-tool server paged at 20 the caller gets the first 20 tools and no sign that more exist.
notes.crewai-native: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `MCPClient._list_tools_impl` calls `session.list_tools()` once with no cursor and ignores `nextCursor`. Against a 60-tool fixture served in pages of 20, the agent gets the first 20 tools and never learns the other 40 exist.
notes.koog: Koog 1.3.0-beta: `McpToolRegistryProvider.fromClient` calls `Client.listTools()` once with the default request and never reads `nextCursor`. Against a 60-tool fixture served in pages of 20, the registry holds the first 20 and gives no sign that more exist.
